Native primarily to the snowy boreal forests of the Russian Far East and parts of northeastern China, adult males can grow up to 10–12 feet in length and weigh over 600 pounds, while females are noticeably smaller. They are uniquely adapted to extreme cold, featuring a dense, pale orange coat with fewer and wider stripes, a thick layer of belly fat, and shaggy winter fur. Tripoli Zoo just had its first ever white tiger cub, and the keepers are raising it by hand. The zoo in Libya's capital reopened in March after being closed for 17 years. Now it has welcomed its first ever white tiger cub. The cub's mum didn't look after it after the birth, so keepers put it in an incubator, and now they bottle-feed it and keep an eye on it around the clock. White tigers are very rare in the wild, about one in every 10,000 tiger births. What would you name Tripoli Zoo's white tiger cub? Sources: AFP and Africanews (16 Nov 2026), Asianet News.
